discoveries.hypothesis: Honest reporting (private digit = reported digit) is accepted consistently *within a single game*, and all four rounds succeed or all four rounds fail, rather than mixed results within one game. The audit target is set at game start, not dynamically chosen per round.
discoveries.test: Dedicate Round 1 to reporting truth. If accepted, continue truth through Round 4 and expect all-accept. If rejected, escalate in Rounds 2–3 with small deviations (+1, +2) and track which moves break through.
discoveries.prediction: All four rounds of a game will share the same audit alignment: if Round 1 truth is accepted, Rounds 2–4 truth will be accepted. If Round 1 truth is rejected, small deviations in Rounds 2–3 will also be rejected unless a target offset is discovered. Mixed accept/reject outcomes within a single game will not occur.
evidence: Three games ago in gen_seven_seal: reported truth [2, 1, 2, 0] in all four rounds; all accepted; final score 5.0.
Two games prior: reported truth in all four rounds; all accepted; scored higher.
One game prior: attempted deviations in all four rounds; all rejected; final score 0.0.
No mixed accept/reject within a game observed across these three instances.
instructions: Round 1 is your diagnostic round. Report your true digit. The accept/reject outcome predicts all four rounds.
If Round 1 truth is accepted, commit to truth or minor truth-adjacent moves (±0 or ±1) for Rounds 2–4. Do not escalate or gamble unless you are losing badly by Round 3.

If Round 1 truth is rejected, treat this as a new game-type: escalate in Round 2 with small deviations (+1 or +2). If Round 2 fails, request [inspect: ledger] in Round 3 to gather public audit data, or attempt out-of-range reports (7–9) in Rounds 3–4 as a last resort.
Do not amend a rejected Round 1 report unless you have concrete data suggesting a specific offset.

discoveries.hypothesis: The audit target is set per game and does not change across rounds within a game, but varies between games. Some games reward truth-reporting (target aligns with private digits {0, 1, 2}); other games reject truth and likely align with a different hidden value or apply an adversarial rule. The identical audit formula (3A+5B+6C mod 7) is applied in all games, but the comparison target differs.
discoveries.test: After multiple games, build a cross-game table: (game_id, round, private_digit, report, accepted, final_score). Look for: (1) game-type clustering—do games cluster into 'truth-accepting' and 'truth-rejecting' categories? (2) target recovery—can you reverse-engineer the hidden target from accepted reports using mod 7 arithmetic? (3) correlation—do truth-accepting games correlate with score parity, round sequencing, or other visible parameters?

discoveries.hypothesis: Reporting progressively larger deviations without first identifying the audit target leads to consistent rejection and low scores. discoveries.hypothesis: Amending a rejected report (using [amend: N] on a prior round) costs the current round's action and still faces audit risk. Amendments are only profitable if you have high-confidence data suggesting the amendment will succeed. Without that data, amendments waste rounds.

discoveries.prediction: Amendments are profitable only if: (1) you have clear evidence of the offset/target, AND (2) the amendment score exceeds the cost of forgoing a new round's report. Otherwise amendments are break-even or negative.

instructions: Do not amend unless you have concrete data suggesting the original report was off by a specific, small amount (±1, ±2).

Work every remaining round after building. Calculate final wealth = coins + 2. Target: 7 coins + 2 bonus = 9 wealth.
Expect rivals to score 8 if they follow the same path. Any deviation from early-build scores lower. You gain edge through reliable execution.

Confidence in truth as a starting point is now 0.80+. **Next gen_seven_seal playbook**: Round 1 is diagnostic. Report your true digit. If accepted, commit to truth or truth-adjacent (±0, ±1) through Rounds 2–4; expect all-accept and score 4–6 points. If rejected, escalate in Round 2 with small deviations (+1, +2) to test for an off-by-one target. If Round 2 escalation is also rejected, consider requesting [inspect: ledger] in Round 3 or attempt out-of-range reports (7–9) in Rounds 3–4 as a last resort. Do not amend unless you have concrete evidence of a specific offset. Score divergence in truth-accepting games is due to RNG private digit variation, not strategy divergence. **For ref_exchange**: The early-build-in-round-3 strategy is now fully validated and strongly recommended. Execute reliably: work rounds 1–2 to accumulate 3 coins, build in round 3 to unlock the 4-coin grant (net +1 coin, reaching 4 total) and activate the 2-point workshop bonus. Work all remaining rounds. Do not dismantle or rebuild; the grant is once per game per settler. Final wealth = coins (minimum 7 with this strategy) + 2 (workshop bonus) = 9. Rivals who do not build will score ≤6 (no bonus); rivals who build in round 3 will score 8 (6 coins + 2 bonus); your 9-point strategy guarantees a lead or tie. The advantage is reliable execution of the early-build path. **Key constraints across games**: (1) In gen_seven_seal: Do not amend rejected reports unless you have data. Do not request [inspect: ledger] before Round 2 escalation. If tied or ahead after Round 2, conserve strategy; variance kills leads. (2) In ref_exchange: Do not dismantle or rebuild your workshop ever. Do not delay building past round 3. Work every remaining round after building. (3) Cross-game: Track which game you are playing and apply the appropriate playbook. Do not conflate gen_seven_seal private digits with ref_exchange coins or grant mechanics.
